questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not use the brakes until you have control of the car. Then brake gently and pull to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
Drive better because they are more careful than sober drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your thinking, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you see:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
A police officer ordering you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your license and paperwork ready before the officer comes to your window.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel. Tell your passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to exit. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Make a complete stop before turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right here.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: The best way to protect yourself in a crash is to use:

options.text: Both a seat belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a seat belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts can double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags work together with seat belts to give you extra protection. Always wear both your shoulder belt and lap belt.

questions.question: What should you do before you turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers about your next move.

questions.question: What can make it unsafe for you to drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be healthy and alert. Alcohol, drugs, and tiredness all make driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to go the wrong way on a one-way street.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning cars on a green light must let oncoming cars pass first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning cars on a green light must let oncoming cars pass first.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left on a green light, they must wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when they are worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Every person in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can be thrown around the car during a crash and hurt other people.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get revenge will make the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep the pedestrian safe.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt while in a moving vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All people in the vehicle
questions.explanation: Everyone in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Police can stop and ticket drivers or passengers who are not wearing one. If a passenger under 16 does not wear a seat belt, the driver gets fined.

questions.question: To turn right, you should be in which lane?

options.text: The lane closest to the direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go, and turn into the lane closest to your current lane.

questions.question: How can you reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, follow posted speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that two-way traffic is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only used in construction zones.
They are red and blue in color.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give drivers helpful information.
questions.explanation: Highway markings provide information for drivers. They help drivers stay in the correct position, show safe passing areas, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other vehicles are visible.
Signal only if other vehicles are visible.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other vehicles are visible.
questions.explanation: Always use your signal when changing lanes, turning, or moving away from a curb. Do not skip this important safety step.

questions.question: What is most important when backing up your car?

options.text: Look behind your car carefully and give way to other vehicles and pedestrians.
Keep one foot on the brake while backing.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind your car carefully and give way to other vehicles and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, look directly through the rear window to check for hazards. Do not rely only on your mirrors. Look left and right and yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: If you see side-by-side red lights flashing at a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and cross the railroad.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean you must stop.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check both mirrors to see traffic behind you. Before moving, turn your head and check your blind spot for any vehicles you cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving.
questions.explanation: Tiredness while driving is as dangerous as driving drunk. Stop driving if you feel tired.
